verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving: I traced every error path, the empty-bare-value case and the end-of-stream handling in each, and they match the original. B also commits 18 regression tests that pin every error kind with its exact position, plus the edge cases (empty values, a trailing backslash, non-ASCII text, iteration after an error or end of line). That protection is lasting, which matters for a refactor whose main requirement is identical output. A's equivalence checking happened only in a scratch directory outside the repo, which it also left behind, so the repo gains no protection against future regressions.
a_issues: No tests added to the repo: the old-vs-new comparison and the benchmark live in `..\scratch\` and will not guard future edits to the tokenizer.
Leaves scratch files on disk next to the repo for the developer to clean up.
Uses `#[inline]` on every helper without showing it is needed (minor).
b_issues: The `Scanned` struct adds a little indirection compared with mutating `self` directly (minor).
Several `scan_*` functions have no doc comments, unlike A's.
`pos` is no longer moved to the end of the line after an error; this is disclosed and not observable through the iterator.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors are behavior-preserving as far as I can trace: same error kinds and positions, empty bare values, and the stream stays finished after an error. A also adds 18 regression tests to the repo that pin every error variant with exact positions, plus edge cases like non-ASCII text and a trailing backslash. Those tests protect this refactor and the future format changes the developer is worried about. B's 20M-line differential check is strong, but it lives in an uncommitted scratch directory, so the repo gains no protection.
a_issues: Introduces a `Scanned` struct and closure-taking helper, a bit more indirection than strictly needed
After an error `pos` is no longer moved to the end of the line (internal only, but disclosed)
Benchmark spread is wide (fastest 202–243 ms old vs 220–241 ms new), so 'no slowdown' rests on noisy numbers
b_issues: No tests added to the repo; the differential fuzz harness and benchmark live outside it in `..\scratch\` and are left behind
The key/word and bare-value scanning loops are near-duplicates instead of sharing a helper
Blanket `#[inline]` on every private method adds noise with no shown benefit
